In the theory of [[stochastic process]]es, a '''ν-transform''' is an operation that transforms a [[measure (mathematics)|measure]] or a [[point process]] into a different point process. Intuitively the ν-transform randomly relocates the points of the point process, with the type of relocation being dependent on the position of each point.

== Definition ==
=== For measures ===
Let <math> \delta_x </math> denote the [[Dirac measure]] on the point <math> x </math> and let <math> \mu </math> be a simple point measure on <math> S </math>. This means that
:<math> \mu= \sum_k \delta_{s_k} </math>

for distinct <math> s_k \in S</math> and <math> \mu(B)< \infty </math> for every bounded set <math> B </math> in  <math> S </math>. Further, let <math> \nu </math> be a [[Markov kernel]] from <math> S </math> to <math> T </math>.

Let <math> \tau_k </math> be independent random elements with distribution <math> \nu_{s_k}=\nu(s_k,\cdot) </math>. Then the point process
:<math> \zeta = \sum_{k} \delta_{\tau_k} </math>

is called the ν-transform of the measure <math> \mu </math> if it is locally finite, meaning that <math> \zeta(B) < \infty </math> for every bounded set <math> B </math><ref name="Kallenberg73"/>

=== For point processes ===
For a [[point process]] <math> \xi </math>, a second point process <math> \zeta </math> is called a <math> \nu </math>-transform of <math> \xi </math> if, conditional on <math> \{ \xi=\mu\} </math>, the point process <math> \zeta </math> is a <math> \nu </math>-transform of <math> \mu </math>.<ref name="Kallenberg73"/>

== Properties ==
=== Stability ===
If <math> \zeta </math> is a [[Cox process]] directed by the random measure <math> \xi </math>, then the <math> \nu </math>-transform of <math> \zeta </math> is again a Cox-process, directed by the random measure <math> \xi \cdot \nu </math> (see [[Transition kernel#Composition of kernels]])<ref name="Kallenberg75"/>

Therefore, the <math> \nu </math>-transform of a [[Poisson process]] with intensity measure <math> \mu </math> is a [[Cox process]] directed by a [[random measure]] with distribution <math> \mu \cdot \nu </math>.

=== Laplace transform ===
It <math> \zeta </math> is a <math> \nu </math>-transform of <math> \xi </math>, then the [[Laplace transform]] of <math> \zeta </math> is given by
:<math> \mathcal L_{\zeta}(f)= \exp \left( \int \log \left[ \int \exp(-f(t)) \mu_s(\mathrm dt)\right] \xi(\mathrm ds)\right)</math>

for all bounded, positive and measurable functions <math> f </math>.<ref name="Kallenberg73"/>
